correctness.rationale: At fixed richness, Jaccard is constant across distinct pairs on at most three tips and on four tips at richness other than two (or there is no pair). At richness two the only Jaccard values are 2/3 for overlap and 1 for disjointness. Independently enumerating the 15 pairs of the six communities for each quartet by unions, intersections and symmetric differences of symbolic root-path edge sets reproduced both frozen score multisets and the common-reference witnesses. In the balanced case, f(x)=(2-x)/(3-x) is decreasing and exceeds 2(1-x)/(3-x) on (0,1), so the maximum overlap is f(min(a,b)); the minimum disjoint score is 2(2-a-b)/(4-a-b). Their difference has the stated numerator and positive denominator. Equality therefore gives no strict reversal, and the equal-stem transition is 2−sqrt(2). In the pectinate case the maximum overlap is f(a): f(b) and f(a+b) are smaller, and the other potentially competing term 2(1-b)/(3-a-b) is smaller by a positive difference with numerator (4-a)(b-a)+a. The minimum disjoint score is (4-a-2b)/(4-a-b); the resulting margin is strictly negative because b<1. These exhaust both rooted bifurcating shapes. No numerical grid is used to justify the signs or all-real scope.
residual_risks: The result does not address alternate roots or an ancestral stem, unequal richness, nonultrametric trees, or weighted UniFrac.

value.rationale: The four-tip boundary is intrinsic: four tips at richness two first produce two Jaccard levels, and both bifurcating shapes are classified over their full positive ultrametric length domains. The threshold tells a researcher exactly when branch sharing alone can reverse a presence/absence ordering even at controlled richness; the signed margin and three-community witness distinguish a sharp obstruction from an isolated example or a numerical tie.
residual_risks: This establishes a minimal mathematical phenomenon, not its prevalence in empirical datasets or any biological inference.
